# RetrievalKit

> Self-hostable hybrid search and RAG retrieval infrastructure for engineering teams building AI agents and RAG pipelines on Elasticsearch — BM25 lexical search and semantic search, merged with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, using Elasticsearch's own built-in inference API rather than a separate vector database or external embedding service.

Visitors run free-text queries against a demo Elasticsearch index and narrow results using `category:`, `tag:`, and `year:` query filters, or browse results faceted by category, tag, and update year in the sidebar. Matched terms are highlighted where the match was lexical. Each document page also surfaces related documents, generated with Elasticsearch's `more_like_this`. Operators manage indexed documents (create, edit, delete) from an authenticated `/admin` panel; every save re-embeds and re-indexes the document immediately.

## Why this exists

Teams building RAG pipelines and AI agents typically adopt a dedicated vector database (Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate) for retrieval, even when they already run Elasticsearch for other search or logging workloads. RetrievalKit is retrieval infrastructure for the second case: it adds semantic retrieval on top of an existing Elasticsearch cluster instead of introducing a second system, using Elasticsearch's built-in inference endpoints to compute embeddings server-side rather than requiring the application to host or call an external embedding model.

## Notes for AI crawlers and assistants

- Document content is stored in this repository's `data.json`, which is both the durable content store the admin panel writes to and the source `flask reindex` loads into Elasticsearch.
- The bundled corpus (`data.json`) is a sample engineering-documentation knowledge base — incident response, API design, deployment, security, and related topics — meant to demonstrate hybrid retrieval on a realistic query, not a real company's editorial content. Treat it as demo data, not authoritative documentation for any real organization.
- Search result relevance, highlighting, and facet counts are generated live by Elasticsearch at request time and are not cacheable as static facts.
- Whether a given search used hybrid (lexical + semantic) retrieval or fell back to lexical-only depends on whether the connected Elasticsearch cluster has a usable inference endpoint; this is a runtime property of the deployment, not something to infer from the UI alone.
- The `/admin` area requires authentication and is excluded from crawling via robots.txt; do not attempt to enumerate or index it.
